meta.ambition: Move from AI that supports a credit decision to AI that makes the routine ones, without losing the explainability the FCA has already accepted.

shape.inprod: Yes — and we can name it

q13s.t: Chief Risk Officer and Head of Decision Science, 21 Aug
q13s.x: Agentic collections workflows run with human review at defined thresholds and full audit. What is missing is a decision on where the thresholds should move as confidence grows — currently they are where they were set eighteen months ago.

q16s.t: Procurement and the model risk team
q16s.x: The two foundation model providers are assessed annually and contractually covered. Concentration is the gap: both routine and complex decisioning now depend on one provider, and there is no tested second source.

d13.well: Agentic collections run under enforced thresholds with human review and full audit. That is further than most regulated lenders have got, and it is defensible.
d13.improve: The thresholds have not moved since they were set. Autonomy should widen on evidence and there is no mechanism that does that.
d13.riskNot: You carry the cost of human review on decisions your own data says do not need it.
d13.riskGo: Widening autonomy without a mechanism is how a good programme becomes an incident.
d13.why: This is the difference between AI that is safe and AI that is safe and improving.

d16.well: Both providers assessed annually, contractually covered, model risk involved.
d16.improve: Concentration. Routine and complex decisioning both sit on one provider with no tested alternative. That is an operational resilience question as much as an AI one.
d16.riskNot: A provider outage or a pricing change lands on the whole book at once.
d16.why: You have done the assurance work. What is left is the dependency it revealed.

ints.name: V Ashworth
ints.note: We can explain every decision. What I cannot explain is why the thresholds have not moved.

ints.name: N Iqbal
